candidate: Native guard hooks in .cursor/hooks.json (hooks schema version 1; docs describe editor 3.27 and CLI v2026.10.22)
what: Register the kit's guard for three native events: beforeShellExecution for shell commands, beforeReadFile for file reads, and preToolUse with a matcher for Write, Delete, Grep, Task and MCP tools.
problem_here: The rule checker is wired only to Claude Code's PreToolUse. Cursor needs its own registration, and the guard must read three payload shapes instead of one.
mechanism: Project file .cursor/hooks.json with entries {command, timeout, matcher, failClosed}. The hook gets JSON on stdin and answers {permission: allow or deny, user_message, agent_message}, or exits with code 2 to block. Project hooks run from the project root in a trusted workspace; on Windows the editor runs the command through PowerShell. The same file is read by the terminal agent and, for most events, by cloud agents.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (read 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11; vendor documentation, not measured). Terminal-agent coverage: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (vendor) and one third-party live test, https://github.com/pickypg/ai-agent-macropad/blob/main/cursor/README.md (2026-08-23, Unverified).
maturity: First version not re-checked; terminal-agent support since Jan 2026; still changing in every recent release (3.24 to 3.27). Proprietary. Adoption signal: vendor-documented and targeted by third-party security adapters.
cost: Complexity medium (three shapes, PowerShell invocation, interpreter name). Money none. Failure modes: fail-open default, stdout race, ask not enforced, undocumented tool_input keys for Read, Write and Delete, terminal agent on Windows rejecting every call when started from Git Bash. Attack surface: a hook file in a repository executes code once the workspace is trusted.
simpler_alternative: Let Cursor auto-load the existing Claude Code hook registration (rejected in its own line).
reason: It is the only mechanical enforcement point that exists in both the editor and the terminal agent, and deny is dependable when sent as exit code 2 with failClosed.
cheap_local_trial: Install a canary rule that denies any command, read or edit containing a fixed marker string; trigger each in the editor and in the terminal agent's print mode; confirm the block and save each received payload as a dated fixture.

candidate: Claude Code hook compatibility loader as the Cursor guard (Third-Party Imports setting, on by default; docs as of 2026-11-11)
what: Cursor reads .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json and ~/.claude/settings.json and runs their hooks, mapping PreToolUse to preToolUse and Bash to Shell.
problem_here: It would give a Cursor port for free, because the kit already installs a Claude Code PreToolUse guard. It also runs whether the kit wants it or not.
mechanism: Event and tool-name mapping; accepts hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; exit code 2 blocks; every other failure fails open; Glob is not mapped; onFailure is not mentioned; the input shape delivered to the script is not documented.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/reference/third-party-hooks (read 2026-11-11, vendor documentation). User report that the script receives tool name Shell, not Bash: https://forum.cursor.com/t/support-authoritative-allow-deny-and-ask-verdicts-from-hooks/161342 (2026-11-05, user-generated, Unverified). Reading of the kit's guard code (2026-11-11): an unknown tool name gives exit 0 with no output. Vendor advisory GHSA-pc9j-3qc2-95wv (2026-05-21) concerned this loader.
maturity: Present since at least Jan 2026 (CLI changelog); SDK 1.0.40 (late Oct 2026) only then made Claude-format denies block in local SDK agents. Proprietary.
cost: No build cost, high risk: silent allow of every shell command if tool_name is Shell; the bash-style default expansion and python3 in the registered command fail under PowerShell on Windows and then fail open; ask is not enforced on preToolUse; the user can switch the import off.
simpler_alternative: None simpler; the safe alternative is native hooks plus a guard that recognises a Cursor caller.
reason: Fail-open behaviour and unmapped tools make it advice, not enforcement. Because it runs anyway, the guard must detect a Cursor caller and behave safely.
cheap_local_trial: Open a repository that has only the Claude install in Cursor, run a shell command the guard should deny, and record whether it is blocked and what JSON the script received.

candidate: Answer deny wherever the guard would answer ask (Cursor port rule)
what: The Cursor adapter converts every ask verdict to deny, with a message telling the agent and the user how the user can run the action themselves.
problem_here: The guard uses ask for risky but legitimate actions; on Cursor an ask may never reach a person.
mechanism: preToolUse: ask is accepted by the schema but not enforced. beforeShellExecution: ask is reported not to be applied in Auto-review mode (the default since 3.6) and to prompt only in Allowlist and Run Everything. subagentStart: ask is treated as deny. Print mode: a missing approval becomes a rejection. No payload carries the run mode, so the hook cannot tell which case it is in.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11, vendor documentation: preToolUse ask not enforced). https://forum.cursor.com/t/beforeshellexecution-hook-returning-ask-is-ignored-in-auto-review-mode-honoured-in-allowlist-and-run-everything-3-21-16/173694 (2026-10-05, apparent staff reply, Unverified).
maturity: n/a (rule in the kit). The product gap has been open since at least May 2026.
cost: Low. Failure mode: more friction for attended editor users, who must run a blocked command themselves. No attack surface.
simpler_alternative: Return ask and document that it may not prompt (rejected: silent allow in the default mode).
reason: Matches the upgrade rule that a port answers deny wherever an ask would not reach a person; the hook cannot detect the mode.
cheap_local_trial: Return ask from a canary beforeShellExecution hook in each run mode and in print mode; record whether a prompt appears.

candidate: Deny by exit code 2 with failClosed: true on every guard hook, plus flushed JSON and a short pause before exit
what: The guard signals a block with process exit code 2 and also prints the JSON answer; every guard entry sets failClosed: true; on allow it prints a valid JSON object, flushes, waits about 150 ms and exits 0.
problem_here: Cursor hooks fail open by default, and a known race can lose a fast hook's stdout, so a JSON-only deny can be dropped.
mechanism: Docs: exit 2 equals permission deny; failClosed blocks on crash, timeout, non-zero exit and no output; invalid JSON from a permission hook blocks. With failClosed an empty read blocks instead of allowing.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Race: https://forum.cursor.com/t/race-condition-silently-disables-hooks-that-exit-quickly/165818 (2026-07-16) and https://forum.cursor.com/t/pretooluse-hook-exit-0-but-empty-stdout-under-concurrent-tool-calls-failclosed-blocks/174214 (2026-10-09), both with apparent staff confirmation, Unverified; no fix announced by 2026-11-11.
maturity: failClosed is in the current docs; first version unknown and probably later than the installed 3.2.16 (Unverified).
cost: Low. Failure modes: spurious blocks of allowed calls under parallel tool calls; about 150 ms added per tool call; if the interpreter is missing, every guarded tool call is blocked. No new attack surface.
simpler_alternative: JSON-only answers with the default fail-open (rejected).
reason: Makes the worst case a false block instead of a missed block, which is the order of the quality attributes in the brief.
cheap_local_trial: Send 50 parallel tool calls through a canary hook with and without the pause; count dropped denies and false blocks.

candidate: One guard core with a thin per-agent payload adapter that refuses unknown shapes
what: The guard entry point detects the caller (hook_event_name and cursor_version fields, or CURSOR_VERSION in the environment), maps Cursor shapes (command and cwd; file_path and content; tool_name Shell, Read, Write, Delete, Grep, Task, MCP:name) onto the kit's internal check, and denies when the shape or the tool name is not recognised.
problem_here: Today the guard exits 0 silently on invalid JSON, a missing tool_name or an unknown tool name; all three happen when Cursor calls it.
mechanism: Cursor sends hook_event_name and cursor_version on every hook; native beforeShellExecution and beforeReadFile payloads have no tool_name; preToolUse uses Cursor tool names. The same script is also invoked by Cursor through the Claude-format loader, so it must recognise that case and either apply the Cursor mapping or step aside when native hooks are installed.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks and https://cursor.com/docs/reference/third-party-hooks (2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Kit guard code read 2026-11-11. Captured payload differences: https://chrisnas.github.io/posts/2026-08-23_spying-on-cursor-hooks/ (third party, Unverified).
maturity: n/a (kit code). The same adapter-per-agent structure is used by 1Password/agent-hooks (MIT, pushed 2026-11-04).
cost: Medium: fixtures for each event and each agent; a new harmless tool may be blocked after a product update (acceptable: fail closed with a clear message). No money.
simpler_alternative: A separate guard script per agent (duplicates the rule logic).
reason: Removes the silent-allow path the upgrade brief forbids and keeps the agent-specific layer thin.
cheap_local_trial: Feed the verbatim vendor payloads from the note to the guard as test fixtures; each must produce allow or deny, never empty output.

candidate: Cursor subagent files with readonly: true (.cursor/agents/<name>.md)
what: Install the two reviewer roles as Cursor subagents whose frontmatter sets readonly: true.
problem_here: The reviewers are read-only through Claude-only frontmatter (a tools list and a per-agent hook), which Cursor does not document as honoured.
mechanism: Markdown with frontmatter name, description, model, readonly, is_background. readonly true means no file edits and no state-changing shell commands. .cursor/agents wins over .claude/agents on a name clash. Works in the editor, the terminal agent and cloud agents according to the docs.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/subagents (2026-11-11, vendor documentation; nobody measured how strict readonly is against shell writes).
maturity: In the terminal agent since Mar 2026 (CLI changelog); fixes still landing (v2026.10.17, v2026.10.22). Proprietary.
cost: Low. Failure modes: strength of readonly against shell redirection unknown; the model field may be overridden or fall back; a same-named Claude file is shadowed, so two copies must stay in sync; subagentStart hooks are reported not to fire in the terminal agent. A subagent inherits all parent tools including MCP.
simpler_alternative: Let Cursor discover the existing .claude/agents files (read-only by instruction only).
reason: It is the only documented mechanical read-only switch and keeps a reviewer from changing what it reviews.
cheap_local_trial: Ask the readonly subagent to append a line to a scratch file by edit and by shell redirection; both must fail.

candidate: sessionStart hook returning additional_context
what: Run the kit's status script at session start and inject its short status text into the conversation.
problem_here: The kit shows run and journal status at session start on Claude Code; Cursor needs an equivalent.
mechanism: sessionStart input has session_id, is_background_agent, composer_mode; output may carry env and additional_context; fire-and-forget, cannot block. Not available in cloud agents.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Terminal-agent support: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (Jan 2026) and apparent staff on https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-cli-doesnt-send-all-events-defined-in-hooks/148316 (2026-04-12, Unverified).
maturity: Documented. Proprietary.
cost: Low. Failure modes: context may not be injected on older builds; no sessionStart for subagent sessions (third-party observation); adds tokens to every session. No money.
simpler_alternative: One line in AGENTS.md telling the agent to run the status command first (instruction only).
reason: Cheap, mechanical and the same script as the Claude port; fall back to the AGENTS.md line where it does not fire.
cheap_local_trial: The hook prints a unique token as additional_context; ask the agent to repeat the token in the editor and in print mode.

candidate: Terminal-agent statusLine command (global cli-config.json; seen on CLI 2026.07.20)
what: Custom status line fed by a command that receives session JSON on stdin.
problem_here: The kit has a Claude Code status line showing run state; a Cursor port would want the same.
mechanism: statusLine: {type: command, command, padding} in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json; the payload includes context_window token counts and autorun; it replaces the native footer. The editor has no equivalent.
evidence: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-cli-custom-statusline-replaces-native-footer-and-cannot-preserve-auto-review-state/166364 (2026-07-22 to 2026-07-27, apparent staff, Unverified); feature announced in https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (Apr 2026); absent from https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/configuration (2026-11-11).
maturity: About 7 months old; schema undocumented. Proprietary.
cost: Little code, but it must be written to the user's home config, which the installer may not touch without an explicit flag; an active session can overwrite the file on exit; it hides the native footer including the run-mode indicator.
simpler_alternative: No status line on Cursor; the status command and the sessionStart text cover it.
reason: Global, undocumented and footer-replacing; the value is cosmetic.
cheap_local_trial: With an explicit opt-in flag, add the block to a copy of the config under CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR and start an interactive session.

candidate: Single skill root for Cursor: reuse the installed .claude/skills/nn-training instead of a second copy
what: Decide where the skill lives for Cursor: (a) rely on discovery of .claude/skills, (b) copy to .agents/skills, (c) copy to .cursor/skills.
problem_here: Cursor reads .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .claude/skills and .codex/skills. A second copy may be listed twice and the copies can drift; native Windows has no symbolic links. If another port installs the skill under .agents/skills, Cursor sees two copies.
mechanism: SKILL.md with name equal to the folder name, description up to 1,024 characters, body up to about 5,000 tokens, references loaded on demand; /skill-name works in the editor and in print mode.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/skills (2026-11-11, vendor documentation); limits from https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes (3.25) and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (v2026.10.08). Precedence between roots is not documented (Unverified).
maturity: Open skill format used by several agents; in the Cursor terminal agent since Mar 2026. Proprietary product, open format.
cost: Low. Failure modes: duplicate listing; discovery of .claude/skills stops if the user turns Third-Party Imports off; a skill body over the token limit raises a warning. No money.
simpler_alternative: No skill on Cursor and the whole procedure in AGENTS.md (too long for always-on context).
reason: One copy avoids drift, but it depends on a default-on setting and undocumented precedence, so try it before fixing the layout.
cheap_local_trial: Open a repository with the skill in .claude/skills only, then with a second copy in .agents/skills; list skills in the editor and in the terminal agent and note duplicates.

candidate: Root AGENTS.md instruction block (marked, idempotent)
what: Short always-on block pointing to the skill, the run controller and the hard rules, between begin and end markers so the installer can update it.
problem_here: Cursor needs an always-loaded instruction; the kit today writes only a CLAUDE.md block.
mechanism: The editor, the terminal agent and cloud agents read root AGENTS.md; nested files combine with parents. The terminal agent also reads root CLAUDE.md.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/rules and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using (2026-11-11, vendor documentation); duplicate-injection fix in https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes (Week of Oct 12, 2026).
maturity: Cross-vendor convention; first Cursor version not checked. Proprietary product, open convention.
cost: Low. Failure modes: a block present in both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md reaches the model twice on older builds; a user-owned AGENTS.md must be merged, not overwritten; instruction only, nothing is enforced.
simpler_alternative: None; this is the simplest.
reason: One file serves Cursor's three surfaces and other agents that read AGENTS.md; keep it short and the same in meaning as the CLAUDE.md block.
cheap_local_trial: Put a unique token in the block and ask each surface which token its instructions contain.

candidate: Project rule .cursor/rules/nn-training.mdc with alwaysApply: true
what: Cursor-native always-on rule file carrying the same short instruction block.
problem_here: Alternative home for the always-on instructions.
mechanism: Files must end in .mdc (plain .md is ignored); frontmatter description, globs, alwaysApply; alwaysApply true ignores globs and description; globs attach the rule when a matching file is in context. Read by the editor and the terminal agent.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/rules (2026-11-11, vendor documentation, not measured).
maturity: Long-standing feature (first version not re-checked). Proprietary format.
cost: Low. Failure modes: a second always-on copy next to AGENTS.md doubles instruction tokens; the format is Cursor-only; rule matching on Windows was still being fixed in Oct 2026 (CLI v2026.10.17).
simpler_alternative: Root AGENTS.md block.
reason: Adds nothing over AGENTS.md for an always-on block. Revisit only for glob-scoped reminders, for example attaching evaluation rules when evaluator files are in context.
cheap_local_trial: Not needed unless glob-scoped rules are wanted; then add one rule with a glob and check that it attaches when a matching file is opened.

candidate: Project MCP config .cursor/mcp.json, written only when an optional MCP module is enabled
what: Template entry under mcpServers for any optional server the kit offers (none in core).
problem_here: Optional modules that expose an MCP server need a Cursor registration next to the Claude one.
mechanism: JSON {mcpServers: {name: {command, args, env}}} or {url, headers}; interpolation ${env:NAME}, ${userHome}, ${workspaceFolder}; project file .cursor/mcp.json, user file ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Connections need approval; in the terminal agent, project servers need approval or --approve-mcps.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/mcp and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (2026-11-10, vendor documentation, not measured).
maturity: Mature in the editor; terminal-agent MCP management is in the CLI changelog. Proprietary product, open protocol.
cost: Low. Failure modes: unattended runs reject calls when a project server is not approved; secrets must come from ${env:NAME} and never be written into the file; MCP hooks do not run in cloud agents. Attack surface: every MCP server widens what injected text can reach.
simpler_alternative: Call the kit's command-line tools through the shell (current design, no MCP).
reason: Needed only by optional modules; the format is simple and documented. Core stays without MCP.
cheap_local_trial: Register a trivial local stdio server in a scratch project and call one tool from the editor and from the terminal agent.

candidate: Terminal-agent permission file <project>/.cursor/cli.json (permissions.allow and permissions.deny)
what: Project-level allow and deny lists for the terminal agent, translated from the kit's Claude Code permission rules.
problem_here: The kit ships allow, ask and deny rules for Claude Code; the terminal agent has its own syntax and no ask tier.
mechanism: Tokens Shell(commandBase), Read(pathOrGlob), Write(pathOrGlob), WebFetch(domain), Mcp(server:tool); deny wins over allow; only permissions may be set at project level, everything else lives in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json. In print mode without --force a shell command that is not allowed is reported to be rejected without a prompt.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/configuration (2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Print-mode behaviour: https://forum.cursor.com/t/disable-permissions-ask-in-sandbox/157243 (2026-04-13, apparent staff, Unverified).
maturity: Documented; WebFetch allow rules were not honoured in print mode on CLI 2026.09.18 (acknowledged bug). Proprietary.
cost: Low. Failure modes: no ask tier, no Delete token, Shell() matches by command base so an allowed interpreter can run any script; conflicting statements on whether the terminal agent also reads permissions.json; a user's existing file must be merged. Attack surface: an over-broad allow entry removes the only gate in unattended runs.
simpler_alternative: No file; rely on hooks alone (loses the allowlist that makes unattended runs possible without --force).
reason: It is the documented way to let the controller commands run unattended while everything else is rejected; ask rules move into the guard as denies.
cheap_local_trial: With only the controller's read-only commands allowed, run print mode on a prompt that needs one allowed and one disallowed command; confirm the second is rejected and the run still ends.

candidate: Editor allowlist file .cursor/permissions.json (terminalAllowlist, mcpAllowlist, autoRun)
what: Project-level allowlist for commands and MCP tools the editor agent may run without asking, plus natural-language hints for Auto-review.
problem_here: It would let the kit's read-only controller commands run without a prompt in the editor, as the Claude Code allow rules do.
mechanism: JSON in ~/.cursor/ or <project>/.cursor/; terminalAllowlist holds command prefixes, mcpAllowlist holds server:tool, autoRun holds allow_instructions and block_instructions. The file overrides the in-app allowlist. The vendor calls it 'not a security boundary'. There are no deny or ask lists.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/reference/permissions (2026-11-10, vendor documentation). Vendor advisories on allowlist bypass: GHSA-82wg-qcm4-fp2w (2026-01-14) and GHSA-hf2x-r83r-qw5q (2026-03-09) at https://github.com/cursor/cursor/security/advisories (2026-11-11).
maturity: First version not captured; behaviour still being fixed in 3.26. Proprietary.
cost: Little code. Failure modes: a project file replaces the user's own in-app allowlist, a surprise the installer would cause; prefix matching; allowlisted commands have skipped hook ask answers in past versions. Attack surface: widens auto-run.
simpler_alternative: Ship nothing; the user approves controller commands or adds them in the app.
reason: Convenience only, not a boundary, and it overrides a user's settings; offer as a documented snippet instead of installing it.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch project add one prefix and check whether the user's in-app allowlist entries still apply.

candidate: Agent sandbox for unattended runs (--sandbox enabled; sandbox.json; CLI v2026.10.22)
what: Run the terminal agent's shell commands inside the vendor sandbox: writes limited to the workspace, network blocked by default, protected paths read-only.
problem_here: The unattended loop needs the narrowest permissions the agent offers, without bypassing approvals outside a container.
mechanism: macOS Seatbelt; Linux Landlock plus seccomp; on Windows the Linux sandbox runs inside WSL2 and there is no native Windows sandbox. Flag --sandbox enabled or disabled; settings sandbox.mode, sandbox.networkAccess, sandbox.readBoundary in the global config and sandbox.json per project. The terminal agent fails fast when the sandbox is requested but unavailable.
evidence: https://cursor.com/blog/agent-sandboxing (2026-02-18, vendor blog; vendor-measured claim that sandboxed agents stop 40% less often), https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (2026-11-10). Escapes fixed in 2026: CVE-2026-50548, CVE-2026-50549, CVE-2026-73217; CVE-2026-73218 lists no patched version (https://github.com/cursor/cursor/security/advisories , 2026-11-11).
maturity: Described by the vendor in Feb 2026; several critical escapes patched within the year. Proprietary.
cost: Complexity low to medium. Failure modes: GPU access inside the sandbox is untested; training needs network for datasets unless they are cached; unavailable on native Windows; with Run Everything the sandbox is off. Attack surface: the sandbox is the boundary and it has a recent escape history.
simpler_alternative: Allowlist plus hooks only (the only option on native Windows).
reason: Narrowest documented unattended mode on Linux, macOS and WSL2, but GPU training inside it is unproven; try it before the loop depends on it.
cheap_local_trial: Under WSL2, run print mode with --sandbox enabled on a prompt that starts a one-minute GPU run through the controller; check GPU visibility, write locations and that a write outside the workspace fails.

candidate: .cursorignore entry for sealed test data
what: List the held-out test set and other sealed paths in the project's ignore file so the agent's file tools cannot read them.
problem_here: The test set must stay unread until the final evaluation; the guard blocks reads by hook, and a second independent barrier is cheap.
mechanism: Root .cursorignore with gitignore syntax; ignored files are blocked from the agent's read and search tools and, in the Linux sandbox, are inaccessible to sandboxed processes. Terminal commands and MCP tools outside the sandbox are not covered. The file itself is a protected path.
evidence: https://cursor.com/help/customization/ignore-files and https://cursor.com/blog/agent-sandboxing (2026-11-10, vendor documentation, not measured); CLI v2026.10.15 note that ignore and Read deny rules also apply outside the workspace (https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes , 2026-11-11).
maturity: Long-standing feature. Proprietary. Advisories from 2025 show path-quirk bypasses on Windows (GHSA-2jr2-8wf5-v6pf, GHSA-6r98-6qcw-rxrw).
cost: Low. Failure modes: a shell command still reads the file outside the sandbox; inside the sandbox the final evaluation could not read the test set either, so the evaluator must run outside the agent; the user's own ignore file must be merged. No money.
simpler_alternative: Guard hook only.
reason: Independent second barrier for the top-ranked quality attribute, but its interaction with the final evaluation needs a test.
cheap_local_trial: Add a dummy sealed file, then ask the agent to read it with the read tool, with search and with a shell command, sandbox on and off; record which paths are blocked.

candidate: Unattended driver: cursor-agent -p --trust --output-format stream-json with a project allowlist and no --force (CLI v2026.10.22)
what: The harness-owned loop starts one terminal-agent process per iteration in print mode and reads the event stream.
problem_here: The research loop must run with nobody to answer prompts, with the narrowest permissions, and must tell success from a run in which everything was rejected.
mechanism: -p gives all tools; --trust accepts the workspace in headless mode; without --force, shell commands outside the allowlist are reported to be rejected without a prompt and deletes are always rejected; file writes are applied. Output: json has type, subtype, is_error, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, result, session_id, request_id; stream-json adds system init, assistant, tool_call and result events; failure is a non-zero exit with no JSON.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters , https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/output-format , https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless (2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Behaviour without --force: apparent staff on https://forum.cursor.com/t/disable-permissions-ask-in-sandbox/157243 (2026-04-13) and https://forum.cursor.com/t/cli-allowlist-cannot-auto-approve-deletetoolcall-or-webfetch-skipapproval-stays-false-print-mode-user-rejected/172763 (2026-09-24), Unverified. Not run here.
maturity: Auto-updating binary with date versions, several releases a month. Proprietary; needs a vendor account and network.
cost: Complexity medium. Money: model usage on the user's plan. Failure modes: exit code 0 with subtype success even when every tool call was rejected; docs disagree on whether writes apply without --force; token usage fields undocumented; administrators can disable headless mode; auto-update can change behaviour in the middle of a loop. Attack surface: the agent can edit any workspace file without approval.
simpler_alternative: Attended use only on Cursor, with the loop offered on other agents first.
reason: It is the vendor-suggested unattended form that does not bypass approvals; too much of its behaviour is unverified to adopt without a recorded trial.
cheap_local_trial: One print-mode run on a scratch repository with a prompt that edits a file, runs an allowed command, runs a disallowed command and deletes a file; save the full stream, the exit code and the resulting file tree.

candidate: --force / --yolo (approve everything) for unattended runs
what: Flag that auto-approves shell commands, writes, deletes and MCP calls unless explicitly denied.
problem_here: It is the shortest way to make an unattended run finish.
mechanism: -f, --force: 'Force allow commands unless explicitly denied'; --yolo is an alias; comparable to approvalMode unrestricted; with Run Everything the sandbox is off unless permissions.json restricts it.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters and https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes (3.24) (2026-11-11, vendor documentation). Apparent staff: --force 'also auto-approves shell, writes, and deletes, so use it only in a workspace you trust' (https://forum.cursor.com/t/cli-allowlist-cannot-auto-approve-deletetoolcall-or-webfetch-skipapproval-stays-false-print-mode-user-rejected/172763 , 2026-09-24, Unverified).
maturity: Stable flag. Proprietary.
cost: No build cost. Failure modes: any injected or mistaken command runs; deny rules and hooks become the only barrier, and hooks have a fail-open and race history. Attack surface: maximal.
simpler_alternative: Print mode with an allowlist and no --force.
reason: The brief forbids bypassing approvals for unattended work outside an isolated container. Permit it only inside an optional container mode, never on the host.
cheap_local_trial: None on the host. In a throwaway container only: confirm deny rules in cli.json still hold under --force.

candidate: stop hook followup_message as the loop engine

simpler_alternative: Harness-owned loop that starts a fresh agent process per iteration.

candidate: Install-time self-test that captures real hook payloads (doctor command)

candidate: Start the terminal agent as cursor-agent, from PowerShell or cmd on Windows
what: The loop and the docs call the binary by its alias cursor-agent and, on native Windows, start it from PowerShell or cmd, never from Git Bash.
problem_here: The name agent collides with other tools; started from Git Bash on Windows the terminal agent is reported to fail every hook and reject every tool call while still exiting 0.

simpler_alternative: Call agent and let the user sort out collisions.
reason: Free, and avoids two failure modes that look like success.
cheap_local_trial: When a terminal agent is installed: run cursor-agent --version from PowerShell and from Git Bash, and one hooked command in each.

candidate: WSL2 as the supported route for unattended Cursor runs on Windows

problem_here: Native Windows is a first-class platform for the kit, but the vendor sandbox does not exist there and terminal-agent hooks have open Windows issues.

Windows hook issues: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-agent-on-windows-launched-from-git-bash-rejects-every-hook-the-powershell-wrapper-is-run-with-bash-eval/172789 and https://forum.cursor.com/t/cli-hooks-block-each-tool-call-for-the-full-timeout-lowering-it-silently-disables-deny-hooks-windows/169942 (Unverified).

problem_here: Print mode otherwise has full write access even without --force; read-only steps do not need it.

maturity: Flag documented. Proprietary.
cost: Low. Failure modes: unknown shell behaviour in these modes; a 15-second auto-reject on mode-switch requests; the model may answer that it cannot complete the task.
simpler_alternative: Use the readonly subagent inside a normal run.

cheap_local_trial: Print-mode run with --mode ask on a prompt that tries to edit a file and run a command; record both outcomes.

problem_here: Relevant only if an optional module adds an MCP server, or the user's repository already has servers that could read sealed data.

reason: Core has no MCP server; add it with the first optional module that needs it.
cheap_local_trial: None now.

candidate: Sign-in handling for unattended runs: reuse the user's existing login, never store a key

problem_here: Headless runs need credentials; the kit must not leak or persist them, and nobody is present to complete a browser login.
